Report template helpers

Source: R/report_helpers.R
report_helpers.Rd

Exported building blocks for report() templates. The shipped templates in inst/templates/ are built on these, and custom user templates should call them (namespace-qualified, e.g. energyRt::report_tbl(...)) instead of re-implementing formatting: they render the same content correctly for the three supported outputs – HTML, Word (docx), and LaTeX/PDF.

Usage

report_output(default = c("html", "word", "latex"))

report_setup(default = c("html", "word", "latex"))

report_layout()

report_esc(x, output = report_output())

report_fmt_val(x, digits = 4L)

report_img(path, frac = 1, output = report_output(), caption = NULL)

report_img_row(paths, frac_total = 1, gap = 0.02, output = report_output())

report_pagebreak(output = report_output())

report_fig_height(p, base = 3.2, per_row = 1.5, max = 9)

report_plot_png(p, w_in, h_in = NULL, dpi = 150)

report_fig(
  p,
  w_in = 7,
  h_in = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  frac = 1,
  dpi = 150,
  output = report_output()
)

report_sec(title, note = NULL, output = report_output())

report_tbl(
  df,
  caption = NULL,
  digits = 4L,
  output = report_output(),
  max_rows = NULL,
  scroll = TRUE
)

report_css(output = report_output())

report_header(
  name,
  desc = "",
  image_file = NULL,
  frac = report_layout()$hdr_img,
  output = report_output()
)

Arguments

default

character, the output assumed when no knitr/pandoc context is available (e.g. interactive use or tests).

x

character or numeric value to escape / format.

output

character, one of "html", "word", "latex". Defaults to auto-detection via report_output(); pass explicitly in tests.

digits

integer, significant digits for numeric formatting.

path

character, path to an image file.

frac

numeric, width as a fraction of the text/line width.

paths

character vector of image paths (missing files dropped).

frac_total

numeric, total line-width fraction a row of images spans.

gap

numeric, fraction of the line width between row images.

p

a ggplot object.

base

numeric, figure height in inches for a single panel row.

per_row

numeric, inches added for every further panel row.

max

numeric, cap on the returned height in inches.

w_in, h_in

numeric, plot size in inches.

dpi

integer, raster resolution.

title, note, caption

character, section / table headings.

df

data.frame to render as a table.

max_rows

integer or NULL: cap the printed rows with a "... K more rows" footer. NULL prints all rows in HTML and caps PDF/Word at a 200-row safety limit.

scroll

logical (HTML only): render tables over 15 rows inside a scrollable box with a sticky header.

name, desc

character, object name and description for the page header.

image_file

character or NULL, optional header image (logo).

Value

report_output() returns the output id invisibly-testable as a character scalar; report_layout() returns a named list of sizing constants; report_plot_png() returns the path to the rendered png; the cat()-based emitters (report_img, report_sec, report_tbl, report_css, report_header) return invisible(NULL) and are meant for results='asis' chunks.

Details

Word must be told apart from LaTeX explicitly: knitr::is_latex_output() is FALSE for docx, but so is is_html_output(), and raw TeX emitted in an "else" branch is silently discarded by pandoc's docx writer. Emitters therefore branch on the three-value output returned by report_output().

Functions

  • report_output(): Detect the current render target: "html", "word", or "latex". Outside a knitr/pandoc context the default is returned.

  • report_setup(): Setup-chunk boilerplate: chunk options (echo/warning/message off) and the per-output knitr.kable.NA placeholder. Returns the detected output invisibly, so templates can open with fmt <- energyRt::report_setup().

  • report_layout(): The one sizing system: named fractions of the text width shared by all outputs, plus the raster dpi.

  • report_esc(): Escape a string for the current output (TeX escaping for "latex", HTML escaping otherwise – Word content goes through pandoc markdown, where HTML entities are safe).

  • report_fmt_val(): Fixed-notation value formatting – never scientific (no "1.2e+03"); "--" for missing.

  • report_img(): Emit an image at a fraction of the line width; the ONLY way images enter a report page. With a caption the image is a pandoc markdown figure (![caption](path) alone in a paragraph): <figure>/<figcaption> in HTML, a numbered figure environment in LaTeX, a captioned figure in Word.

  • report_img_row(): Emit a ROW of images (logos, banners, badges) spanning frac_total of the line width, split evenly with gap between them. Missing files are dropped silently; a single image is capped at half of frac_total so a lone logo does not span the page.

  • report_pagebreak(): Emit a page break: an always-break <div> for HTML (honoured when printing), \newpage for LaTeX, and a raw {=openxml} block for Word. Call from a results='asis' chunk.

  • report_fig_height(): Figure height (inches) from a ggplot's facet layout: base for one panel row, per_row more for every further row, capped at max. Non-ggplot input returns base.

  • report_plot_png(): Rasterise a ggplot at dpi and return the png path (uniform pipeline for all three formats; avoids knitr fig options, which docx partly rejects). h_in = NULL sizes by the facet layout via report_fig_height().

  • report_fig(): Emit a ggplot as a report figure: in-plot title/subtitle are dropped (the document names the figure), the height follows the facet layout unless h_in is given, and caption becomes a pandoc figure caption. NULL plots emit nothing.

  • report_sec(): Section divider + bold title (+ gray note); Word gets a markdown heading.

  • report_tbl(): One table pipeline: prune empty columns, round numerics, kable per format. kable does the escaping (single-escaped, never double). Large tables stay readable: in HTML a table with more than 15 rows renders inside a scrollable box with a sticky header (scroll = FALSE disables); max_rows caps the printed rows with a "... K more rows (of N)" footer – PDF/Word additionally enforce a 200-row safety cap when max_rows is not given.

  • report_css(): Emit the shared report stylesheet (HTML only; a no-op for Word and LaTeX).

  • report_header(): Page header: name + description on the left, optional image (logo) on the right.

Examples

report_esc("a & b", output = "html")
#> [1] "a &amp; b"
report_fmt_val(1234.5678)
#> [1] " 1235"
report_layout()$dpi
#> [1] 150
